name: diagram_types
description: List every diagram and chart type the design system can draw, each with one line on when to use it, plus the semantic patterns (behaviour-first routing) and the import notations. Call it first when drawing, pick ONE type, then call `diagram_guide` for that type. Reads static guide files; changes nothing.

name: diagram_guide
description: Return the instructions for one diagram type. A type with a layout template (`flow`, `pid`) gets the template's data contract with a complete example: write data and draw it with `diagram_render`. Any other type gets the hand-drawing rules (Mantle medium rules, style guide, layout budget, SVG primitives, output sizes) and its own guide; `variant` picks one chart variant. Then this brain's site profile for the type when it keeps one (`files/diagrams/profiles/<type>.md`), fenced as data: its drawing conventions for the type. A long guide comes in parts: read `part` 2 and on when the reply says it continues. Several types in one task? `shared: false` skips the shared rules you already hold. Reads only.

pattern.description: A semantic pattern from `diagram_types` when behaviour carries the meaning, e.g. 'fan-in-queue'. Adds that pattern's rules.

import.description: Redrawing a diagram from another notation: adds its import guide and the fidelity ledger.

mode.description: A type with a layout template (flow, pid): 'template' (the default) gives its data contract; 'draw' the hand-drawing rules.

variant.description: One variant of a chart type, e.g. 'slopegraph' for line, 'dumbbell' for bar.

part.description: The part to read when a reply says the guide continues, e.g. 2.

shared.description: Include the shared rules. False when an earlier call in this task already returned them.

name: diagram_render
description: Lay out and draw a diagram template's data (`flow`: boxes and arrows; `pid`: a P&ID first draft) and return the picture, the data errors and the layout warnings. Saves nothing: the look while you compose. When it is right, save it with `present_create` (same `template` and `data`) and export it for a page with `present_export`. For a hand-drawn diagram type use `diagram_guide`.

data.description: The template data: title, then its nodes, lines and the rest the template guide names.

name: present_list
description: List the owner's Present canvases (agent-written HTML: decks, dashboards, schematics, diagrams), most recently edited first. Optional `query` matches title and text; `tag` filters. For topic search use `search_nodes` with `type='present'`. For one canvas's source use `present_get`.

query.description: substring of the title or text, e.g. 'pump'

tag.description: Only return items carrying this tag.

name: present_get
description: Read one canvas: title, size, rev and its whole HTML `source` (what `present_update` edits). A template canvas also returns its `template` and `data`: change it by passing new `data` to `present_update`, never by editing the source. To see the canvas as a picture use `present_render`. Returns a `url`: cite it as `[title](url)`.

source.description: Include the HTML source: by default yes, except for a template canvas (its data is what you edit).

name: present_render
description: Draw a saved canvas in the browser and return it as a picture, with the errors it raised and the requests it was refused. Saves already return a picture; use this to look again: a later moment of an animation (`at_seconds`), one slide of a deck (`slide`), the dark theme, or another window size for a `fill` canvas. Changes nothing. To look at template data before saving use `diagram_render`.

at_seconds.description: Seconds after load to take the picture, e.g. 4 for the end of an intro.

slide.description: A deck: the slide to show, e.g. 3.

width.description: A fill canvas: window width, e.g. 1280.

height.description: A fill canvas: window height, e.g. 800.

name: present_revisions
description: List the kept past versions of a canvas (the last ten saves), newest first, by rev with their time and size. Bring one back with `present_restore`.

name: present_create
description: Save a new Present canvas and return it drawn as a picture with its errors. Give either `source` (one whole HTML document: the canvas_authoring skill holds the head and library rules) or `template` + `data` for a diagram template (a P&ID, a process flow). Live at once for everyone who can see Present; no draft. A canvas that would not load (a CDN import, an outside URL) is refused with every problem listed. Change one with `present_update`.

template.description: A diagram template instead of source, e.g. 'flow'.

title.description: Display name; defaults to the canvas <title>.

tags.description: Labels, e.g. ['q3-review'].

look.description: Draw the saved canvas and return the picture. False only for a batch of small fixes.

workspace.description: Optional: the id or name of a workspace you moderate to put the new item in (see workspaces_list). Without it the item lands in the folder’s workspace, else in your own private one; the reply says where.

name: present_update
description: Change a canvas and return it drawn as a picture with its errors. Pass ONE of: `edits` (find/replace pairs, each `find` exactly once in the source: the usual fix), `source` (the whole new document), or `data` (a template canvas: its whole new data). `title`/`tags` alone change only the name and labels. Live at once; the last ten versions are kept (`present_revisions`). `if_rev` refuses the save when someone saved since you read it.

find.description: Exact text in the source, long enough to be unique.

replace.description: What replaces it; empty deletes it.

edits.description: Applied in order to the current source.

data.description: A template canvas: the whole new data.

title.description: New display name.

tags.description: Replaces all tags.

look.description: Draw the saved canvas and return the picture. False only for a batch of small fixes.

name: present_restore
description: Bring back a kept past version of a canvas as a new save (nothing is lost: the current version stays in the kept list), and return it drawn. Find the rev with `present_revisions`.

rev.description: The version to bring back, e.g. 3.

name: present_export
description: Write a static copy of a canvas into Files for outside Mantle (an email, a file to send): a template canvas exports the SVG its data draws, any other canvas a PNG picture. Returns the file id and `embed`, the markdown of that copy. To show a canvas in a page of this brain use its `page_embed` from `present_get` instead: it follows the canvas. To update an earlier export, pass the same `filename` with `overwrite: true`: the file id stays, so every embed updates. The canvas stays the editable source: change it with `present_update`, then export again.

filename.description: Stable file name; reuse it to update an export, e.g. 'feed-pump-pid.svg'.

parent_path.description: ltree path of the folder, e.g. 'files.diagrams'.

overwrite.description: Replace the file of the same name: only when it is an earlier export of this canvas.

confirm.description: go ahead although it changes who can see items; only after the user agreed to the changes a first call listed

workspace.description: Optional: the id or name of a workspace you moderate to put the new item in (see workspaces_list). Without it the item lands in the folder’s workspace, else in your own private one; the reply says where.

name: present_delete
description: Permanently delete a canvas with its kept versions and its brain index. Not reversible. Files exported from it stay in Files.

name: canvas_library
description: Return the guide to one library a Present canvas can import, for the exact version this brain serves: the import line, the core API, what changed from versions you may know, the canvas rules (no network, theme tokens, reduced motion) and one complete example canvas that renders. Call it before writing a canvas that uses that library; plain SVG and JS need none. For a mini app pass `for: 'app'`: the import as an app writes it, the React pattern (mount in an effect, clean up, resize, theme) and one complete App.tsx; a library apps cannot use says why. Reads only; changes nothing.

name.description: The library: echarts, d3, three, motion, reveal.js, konva, katex, alpinejs; for an app also diagram-templates.

for.description: Who imports it: a Present canvas, or a mini app's React code.

name: file_create
description: Create or overwrite a **named text file** in a specific folder (e.g. `notes.md`, `config.json`, `recipe.txt`). Use when the user asks for a file with a particular name/extension in a particular place. Filename is lowercased and sanitised automatically. For a plain note that goes into /notes (no filename/folder needed, auto-indexed) use `note_create`. For credentials/passwords use `secret_create`. For a rich-text doc (TipTap) use `page_create`.

parent_path.description: ltree path of the parent folder

content.description: the file's full text — becomes the entire body (replaces, never appends)

overwrite.description: replace the existing file of the same name; default false errors on a name collision

confirm.description: go ahead although it changes who can see items; only after the user agreed to the changes a first call listed

workspace.description: Optional: the id or name of a workspace you moderate to put the new item in (see workspaces_list). Without it the item lands in the folder’s workspace, else in your own private one; the reply says where.

name: folder_get_by_path
description: Look up a folder's metadata + description by its ltree path. For listing what's IN the folder use `folder_list` (sub-folders) or `file_list` (files).

path.description: the folder's full ltree path, e.g. 'files.work.lister-printer'

name: content_supersede
description: Mark a node OUTDATED, optionally naming its replacement — the old copy is down-weighted in retrieval, and when a replacement is named every future hit on it carries a "superseded by" pointer to the successor (a bare mark down-weights only). Returns the updated mark. Use when the user says content is stale, wrong, or replaced ("this file is outdated — the page is the current version"). For deleting content outright use the type's delete tool instead; this is the reversible, history-preserving move. Pass `clear: true` to un-mark (restores full weight); omit `superseded_by` for a bare outdated mark. `page_from_file` / `page_from_note` stamp this automatically; use this for corrections and lineage the system could not see.

node_id.description: the outdated node (file, page, note, … — not emails or folders; those are refused)

superseded_by.description: the node that replaces it, e.g. the corrected page built from a stale file; omit for a bare "outdated" mark

reason.description: why: 'migrated' (content moved to the successor), 'corrected' (the old content is wrong — demotes harder), 'version' (an older export of the same artifact)

clear.description: un-mark instead: clear the supersession and restore full retrieval weight

name: process_extraction
description: Re-fires the pg_notify('node_ingested') signal for any nodes missing data.summary or embedding. Optional `node_id` to target a single node; optional `types` to restrict by node kind; optional `limit` to cap (default 100). Idempotent — already-extracted nodes are short-circuited by the extractor.

limit.description: Max nodes to re-signal in one sweep.

name: find_window
description: Locate WHEN a past topic was discussed. Semantic search over conversation digests (the rolled-up summaries of older chats) and archived chat threads (one summary per chat the user closed with New chat; kind 'thread', with its thread_id), returning candidate time windows each with a topic, summary, and period_start/period_end. Use this first when the user vaguely remembers discussing something ('last week we talked about a Bible topic') but not exactly when, then call `replay_window` with the best window's dates to read the actual turns. Optional `from`/`to` (YYYY-MM-DD or ISO) narrow to a rough date range; omit them to search all of time.

topic.description: what to look for, e.g. 'the Bible discussion about Romans 8'

from.description: optional rough lower bound (YYYY-MM-DD or ISO)

to.description: optional rough upper bound (YYYY-MM-DD or ISO)

name: replay_window
description: Replay the actual raw turns of past conversations within a date range, chronological and lossless (the real words, not a summary). Use after `find_window` has pinned a window, or directly when the user gives a date ('what did we say on Tuesday?'). `from`/`to` accept a bare date (YYYY-MM-DD, widened to the whole day) or a full ISO datetime. If the window is larger than `limit` the result is truncated — narrow the range or pull it in sub-ranges and reason over each. Set `include_traces` to also see what the system actually did in that window (tools run + their results) — useful when the dialogue references work whose details aren't in the words themselves.

surface.description: which conversation surface to pull from

include_traces.description: also return the trace rows whose work ran in this window — what tools/agents ran and what they returned (the hidden working state the dialogue alone does not show)

name: web_search
description: Search the live internet and get a synthesised, cited answer (backed by Perplexity Sonar). Pass a focused natural-language query; returns an `answer` plus the `citations` (source URLs) it relied on. This is the STANDARD, fast/cheap tier — use it for most lookups: current events, latest docs/prices, how-tos, fact-checking a claim. You can call it several times to triangulate. For genuinely hard or conflicting questions use web_search_pro. For the user's OWN past data use search_nodes or recall instead — this only sees the public web.

recency.description: optional: bias toward results no older than this window (for time-sensitive queries)

name: web_search_pro
description: Like web_search but uses a STRONGER, SLOWER model — reserve it for hard, ambiguous, or high-stakes questions, or when standard web_search results conflict or are thin. It costs more and takes noticeably longer, so prefer web_search for routine lookups and reach for this only when the question warrants the extra depth.

recency.description: optional: bias toward results no older than this window (for time-sensitive queries)

name: video_ingest
description: Turn a video into a searchable, timestamped transcript page. Pass `url` for an online video (captions are used when available — free; otherwise the audio is extracted and transcribed via the STT worker), or `file_node_id` for a video file already in Files (always audio + STT). The extracted audio is kept as a file beside the source; `keep_video: true` additionally stores the video itself. For the user's own reference material. Long-running — up to several minutes for an uncaptioned video.

url.description: http(s) link to the video. Exactly one of url / file_node_id.

file_node_id.description: Id of a video file node already in Files. Exactly one of url / file_node_id.

keep_video.description: Also store the full video file (url path only). Default false — disk.

force_stt.description: Skip captions and transcribe the audio even when captions exist.

name: web_map
description: List a website's URLs (sitemap-style discovery) WITHOUT fetching page content. Returns `links` found on the site at `url`, optionally filtered by `search`. Use it to scope a site before `web_crawl` — find how big it is and which subpath holds the content you want. For reading one page into the turn use `web_fetch`; for a synthesised answer use `web_search`. Needs a `firecrawl` API key (/settings/keys) and spends a small amount of Firecrawl credit per call.

url.description: Site or subpath to map, e.g. https://docs.example.com

search.description: Optional keyword filter for the returned links, e.g. 'pricing'.

name: web_crawl
description: Crawl a website and store its pages as searchable documentation. Fetches up to `limit` pages under `url` as clean markdown (JS-rendered, via the Firecrawl cloud) and upserts each into a per-site documentation collection; on a re-crawl, unchanged pages are skipped free. Returns the collection key plus inserted/updated/skipped counts. **Spends Firecrawl credits — roughly one per page — so start small and scope tightly**: run `web_map` first, crawl the deepest `url` that covers the need, and use `include_paths`. For one page use `web_fetch`. Long-running — up to minutes. Needs a `firecrawl` API key (/settings/keys).

url.description: Start URL; the crawl stays under it, so deeper = cheaper (https://example.com/docs beats https://example.com).

limit.description: Max pages to fetch (each costs a credit).

include_paths.description: Only crawl URLs whose path matches one of these regexes, e.g. ['^/docs/'].

exclude_paths.description: Skip URLs whose path matches one of these regexes, e.g. ['/blog/.*'].

name: location_save
description: Persist a place (coordinates + reverse-geocoded address) as a `location` node so future turns near the same spot can reuse it without re-calling the geocoding API. Call this AFTER mapbox_reverse_geocode resolves an address for coordinates you don't already have saved (check location_nearby first). The place is indexed into the brain (searchable via search_nodes). `title` defaults to the address; pass a friendly label (e.g. 'home', 'the office') and `tags` when you know them.

title.description: optional label; defaults to the address

tags.description: Labels for organisation and filtering, e.g. ['work'].

name: location_nearby
description: Return the user's previously-saved `location` places within `radius_meters` of a point, nearest first (with the distance to each). Call this FIRST when you need an address for coordinates — if a saved place is close enough, reuse its address instead of calling the geocoding API. Also answers 'have I been near here before?' / 'what saved places are around me?'. Defaults to the device's current coordinates is NOT automatic — pass the lat/lon you care about (usually the Current location from context).

latitude.description: latitude of the point to search around, e.g. -33.918

longitude.description: longitude of the point to search around, e.g. 18.423

name: location_distance
description: Great-circle (straight-line) distance in metres between two lat/lon points. Use this to answer 'how far is X from me' reliably — do NOT estimate distances from coordinates yourself. Note this is as-the-crow-flies, not travel distance; say so when it matters.

name: route_map
description: Render an overview map PNG of a route and show it inline in the chat. Pass the `polyline` returned by mapbox_directions (its `geometry`, an encoded polyline) plus the origin (`from_longitude`/`from_latitude`) and destination (`to_longitude`/`to_latitude`) for the start/end pins. The path is auto-fitted to the image. Optionally pass `from_label`/`to_label`, `distance_meters`, `duration_seconds`, `profile` to caption it. Call this AFTER mapbox_directions to show the user where a place is and the way there — it's a static overview, not live navigation. Requires a Mapbox key (Settings → API keys, service 'mapbox'); returns the map as an image the user sees inline.

from_label.description: optional caption label for the start (e.g. 'You')

to_label.description: optional caption label for the destination

distance_meters.description: optional route distance for the caption

duration_seconds.description: optional route duration for the caption

name: update_persona
description: Adjust how YOU (the assistant) behave with this user — style, tone, how you address them — ONLY when they explicitly ask for a durable change ('be more professional', 'call me Jay', 'stop using bullet lists'). When the new preference contradicts a persona note already in your context, pass its [ref] in `supersede_refs` so the stale note is retired rather than left to conflict; `remove_refs` drops a behaviour without replacing it. NOT for facts about the user or their world (remembered automatically), and NOT for one-off requests ("just for this reply, be brief") — only changes that should persist across conversations. Acknowledge the change in your reply.

kind.description: style = voice/tone/format; relationship = how you and the user relate (names, in-jokes); correction = fixing a standing mistake.

content.description: One declarative sentence describing the behaviour, e.g. "Prefers a professional, formal tone with no emoji."

add.description: A new persona note to adopt.

supersede_refs.description: The [ref] tags of existing persona notes the new note replaces. They get retired (kept for audit, hidden from future turns).

remove_refs.description: The [ref] tags of existing persona notes to retire without a replacement.

reason.description: Optional short note on why, for the audit trail.

name: set_timezone
description: Change the user's profile timezone. Use when the user is in — or travelling to — a different timezone and the 'Current time:' context line is wrong for where they actually are, or when they ask. If you know their location (the Current location line / a reverse-geocoded city), derive the correct IANA zone yourself and set it. PERSISTENT — all times, event scheduling, reminders, and quiet hours follow it until it's changed back — so say what you changed and offer to switch it back when they head home. Returns the new timezone and the current local time in it so you can confirm.

name: secret_create
description: Capture a sensitive value — password, PIN, API key, recovery code, anything the user explicitly says is private — into the encrypted /secrets store. ALWAYS prefer this over `note_create` or `file_create` for a dictated credential: a note stores it in plaintext where any future tool call can read it, while this seals the value behind a key only the owner's browser session can unlock. The value is REDACTED in trace logs — never echo it back to the user; confirm by title only ('saved your safe PIN'). For multi-field secrets (e.g. a server with both username and password) the /secrets UI is still the right path; this handles the common one-value case.

title.description: short label, e.g. "Safe PIN", "Linode root password"

value.description: the secret value itself — gets encrypted before storage

kind.description: rough category; pick the closest match

label.description: optional field label inside the secret (e.g. 'PIN', 'password'). Defaults to 'value'.

description.description: optional plaintext metadata visible to search (do NOT include the value here)

tags.description: Labels for organisation and filtering, e.g. ['work'].

name: node_share
description: Create (or fetch) the public read-only link to a shareable item (note, task, event, file, app, table, drawing, or folder under files) and return its URL. One link per item; anyone with it can view, no login. It shows the item plus its served list (`serve`): what the item names or embeds, or a folder holds, shows only when on that list. A link is no grant: to show an item to members or clients, grant it to their workspace. Only someone who may edit the item may share it (an app: a home Moderator). For a PAGE prefer `page_share`; to turn a link off use `node_unshare`.

id.description: node id of the item to share (from its listing tool or search_nodes)

mode.description: Always 'public' (the default). Team links are retired.

serve.description: optional: the ids the link shows besides the item (its served list, replacing the one it has): for a page, note, task or event the items it names or embeds (pictures, files, drawings, mentions); for a drawing its images; for a folder the files and subfolders in it. Each must be one you may edit. Without it the list stays as it is (a new link shows the item alone: what it names reads 'Private item'). A file added to a shared folder later is not shown until it is added here.

name: node_unshare
description: Revoke an item's share link: the existing URL stops working immediately. No-op (still succeeds) if it wasn't shared. Changes no one's access in the brain. Works for any shareable item; `page_unshare` is the same for pages.

id.description: node id whose share link to revoke

name: invoke_agent
description: Hand off a single, self-contained prompt to another agent (e.g. a researcher with a stronger model + retrieval tools). Use only when the work would clearly benefit from a different persona or model — not for routing every turn. The child runs once and returns its final text; its conversation history is NOT shared with the parent. Pack the prompt to stand alone: the user's ask (their words, not a paraphrase), the exact node ids via `subject_node_ids`, any composed content IN FULL, and what 'done' looks like. The runtime also attaches the triggering user message automatically as a safety net. The parent agent's `memory_config.delegate_to` must list the target slug, or this call is refused.

agent_slug.description: Slug of the target agent (the `agents.slug` column).

prompt.description: Self-contained instructions for the child. Include any context it needs; the child does not see your conversation history. State the goal, the material (in full — never shortened), and the expected end state.

subject_node_ids.description: Ids of the nodes (pages, tables, files) the child should operate on. Always pass these when the work targets existing content — a child that has to SEARCH for its subject can pick the wrong one.

name: run_plan
description: Create a durable run — a tree of seq/par groups of tool_call, note, worker_invoke, audit, and ask_human items executed in the background — and return its id plus the tree. Use for delegated multi-step jobs worth tracking; for a quick answer or one or two calls, call the tools inline. The default shape for real work: seq( note(plan) → worker_invoke(step) → audit → … ) — every worker step followed by an audit you will judge (via `run_audit`) when resumed. An ask_human step parks the run until the operator answers (pending approvals) — the consent gate for side-effecting phases. You are resumed with compiled results when the run completes. Check progress with `run_state`, extend with `run_append`, stop with `run_cancel`.

title.description: Short human-readable goal, shown in the run view.

budget_usd.description: Auto-pause budget in USD. Crossing it pauses the run mid-flight and asks the operator to raise or cancel (pending approvals). Omit for no budget.

plan.description: The run tree. Node shapes: {kind:'seq'|'par', label?, join_policy?:'wait_all'|'fail_fast', children:[…]} | {kind:'tool_call', tool:'<slug>', args:{…}, side_effecting?:true, timeout_seconds?:600} | {kind:'note', text:'…'} | {kind:'worker_invoke', step:'<self-contained task>', acceptance_criteria?:'…', worker?:'<worker slug — omit for the default>', group?:'<worker group slug — seq-only; expands into par(one attempt per member) + a panel audit; mutually exclusive with worker>', subject_node_ids?:[…]} | {kind:'audit', scope?:'…'} (seq-only, right after the worker step it judges) | {kind:'ask_human', question:'…', options?:['…'], form?:{questions:[{header?:'<chip>', question:'…', options:[{label:'…', description?:'…'}], multi_select?:true, allow_other?:false}]}, timeout_seconds?} (seq-only; waits indefinitely unless timed — the operator answers via pending approvals and the answer flows to later steps; use `form` to ask up to 4 things at once as a questionnaire, plain `options` for one pick-one question). Root must be a group. Mark any state-changing call side_effecting (it then never auto-retries).

name: run_append
description: Append tool_call / note items (or nested groups) to an OPEN group of an existing run; returns the new item ids. Sealed (completed) groups refuse — check `run_state` first and target an open group, or start a new run with `run_plan`. Same node shapes as `run_plan`.

run_id.description: The run to extend (from run_plan or run_state).

group_id.description: Target group item id (defaults to the root group).

children.description: Plan nodes to append, in order.

name: run_state
description: With run_id: return the compiled state of one run — per-item status, one-line outcomes, costs — as text plus structured data. Without run_id: list this brain's recent runs (id, title, status). The compiled state is the ground truth to re-read at resume; never rely on remembered progress.

limit.description: List mode: max runs to return (default 10).

name: run_cancel
description: Cancel a run: every queued/ready/running item in its tree is marked cancelled and no resume fires. Idempotent — cancelling a finished or already-cancelled run reports cancelled=false. In-flight tool executions are not interrupted mid-call; their late results are discarded.

run_id.description: The run to cancel (from run_plan or run_state).

name: run_audit
description: Record your verdict on a pending audit item: 'pass' (advisory findings allowed) advances the run; 'redo' requires at least one blocking finding and supersedes the audited worker step with a fresh attempt carrying your findings (one redo max — a second blocking audit fails the step for human decision). Judge the worker's recorded tool ledger against its claims, not its confidence. Use during a resume turn that presents a pending audit; `run_state` shows which item is waiting.

run_id.description: The run the audit belongs to.

audit_item_id.description: The pending audit item (from the resume prompt or run_state).

verdict.description: 'pass' advances the run; 'redo' reruns the audited step (blocking findings required).

severity.description: blocking = must be fixed (drives redo); advisory = noted, rides along.

claim.description: The specific defect or observation, one sentence.

suggested_fix.description: What the redo should do differently.

findings.description: Your findings. Only blocking severity justifies a redo; advisory rides along into the record.

directive.description: The authoritative instruction for the next step — downstream executes this, it does not re-derive.

name: openrouter_rankings
description: Real-world model popularity: total tokens per model across OpenRouter, aggregated over the requested window (their public top-50 daily dataset). Returns `models` (slug + tokens, busiest first), `asOf`, and the required `attribution` line. Filter by `category` (e.g. 'programming') or `modality` to rank for a specific job. Use with `openrouter_benchmarks` when curating pools — usage says what people trust, benchmarks say what scores. Uses the owner's OpenRouter key.

days.description: Window length ending at the latest completed day.

modality.description: Restrict to traffic of this modality.

name: openrouter_benchmarks
description: Benchmark scores for models, from OpenRouter's benchmarks dataset. `source` picks the shape: 'artificial-analysis' (composite intelligence/coding/agentic indices with pricing), 'design-arena' (ELO/win rates), 'openrouter' (their web-search + classic evals). Filter with `task_type` ('coding', 'intelligence', 'agentic', 'search'). Pair with `openrouter_rankings` when curating: scores + real usage together beat either alone. Uses the owner's OpenRouter key.

name: openrouter_task_classes
description: Market-share breakdown of OpenRouter traffic by task type (code generation, summarization, web search, …) over the last 7 days, including the top models per classification. The fastest way to see which models dominate a specific JOB — useful for the worker pools (summarizer, vision, …). Uses the owner’s OpenRouter key.

name: model_catalog
description: Look up models with pricing: OpenRouter's FULL catalog — chat, image/video generators, speech (TTS) and transcription (STT) engines, embeddings, rerank — each with slug, live input/output $ per 1M, context, `kind`, and `inputModalities`/`outputModalities` (the output side separates an image READER from a GENERATOR). Plus the voice models Mantle reaches through its own adapters (ElevenLabs, Deepgram, AssemblyAI, Google). Pricing is NULL wherever a model is not token-billed — per-minute audio and video routes, those adapter rows — so leave that snapshot empty rather than invent a rate. THE source for slugs and pricing when writing `model_pool_set` entries; each row's `provider` is the route to record. Filter by `kind` per pool; `q` searches name/slug, `ids` fetches exact slugs. Keyless; cached ~5 minutes.

q.description: Substring match on slug or name, e.g. 'sonnet'.

kind.description: What the model must PRODUCE, read from the catalog's output modalities (not from its name). 'chat' = text out.

name: model_pool_list
description: The curated pools and their current entries (name, vendor, per-provider routes, pricing snapshot, rating, note, order) plus each pool’s purpose. Read this FIRST when curating — pools the owner already filled reflect their judgment; say so before replacing entries. The owner sees the same data at /models/pools.

pool.description: One pool id to read, e.g. 'agents'. Omit for all.

name: model_pool_set
description: Upsert one model into a curated pool (matched by pool + name; existing entries are updated in place). `routes` is the model's slug per provider — always include the `openrouter` route, plus the direct-provider slug when it differs (e.g. anthropic 'claude-sonnet-5'). Copy `pricing` from `model_catalog` — it is a snapshot that keeps the $100 comparison working on direct-connected brains. Checked against the live catalog and REFUSED when the model cannot do the pool's job: read `outputModalities` first — one that outputs images is a GENERATOR, never a reader (the Read-images pool wants a capable text-out model that accepts pictures). Curation only: this changes the shortlist at /models/pools, never what any agent or worker runs.

name.description: Display name, e.g. 'Claude Sonnet 5'.

model.description: The slug THAT provider uses for this model.

note.description: Short tier note, e.g. 'flagship' or 'gets the job done'.

position.description: Order in the pool (0 = top; convention: priciest first). Omit to append.

name: model_pool_remove
description: Remove one model from a curated pool, matched by pool + exact name (find both with `model_pool_list`). Only the shortlist changes — nothing that currently uses the model is affected.

pool.description: Pool id the entry lives in.

name.description: Exact display name of the entry.

name: recall_eval
description: Run the brain's retrieval self-check: every golden case (a note tagged `recall-eval-cases`, a JSON array of {id, query, expectNodeIds?|expectTitleIncludes?}) runs through the retrievers agents use (hybrid node and passage search; with passage_scoring's pool set, also the Jev-scored path, about USD 0.0007 per 25 passages per case), is scored (recall@k, MRR), saved as one run note and compared to the previous run. `alert: true` with `reason: 'quality_dropped'` when quality fell, or `reason: 'gold_set_unmatched'` when EVERY case missed both retrievers (repair the gold set, see `unmatchedCases`). `skipped: true, alert: false` when no gold set exists: unmeasured, not degraded, say nothing. Capacity is `brain_capacity`; this measures QUALITY.

name: web_fetch
description: Fetch a URL (API documentation, OpenAPI spec, reference page) and return its readable text. HTML is converted to plain text; JSON/markdown/plain text come back as-is. Long pages are truncated — pass offset to continue reading. Use this to read a service's API docs before authoring tools with api_tool_create.

offset.description: character offset to start from (for paging long documents), default 0

name: api_tool_list
description: List every tool in the registry (builtin, http, shell, recipe, mcp): slug, kind, enabled, requires_confirm, and a short description. Use api_tool_get for full details of one tool.

name: api_tool_get
description: Full definition of one tool by slug: description, input schema, and handler (url/method/headers/query/body templates for http tools).

slug.description: slug of the tool to inspect, e.g. mapbox_geocode

name: api_tool_create
description: Register a new HTTP tool agents can call. Templating: {param} placeholders in url/query/headers/body fill from the tool-call input (URL-encoded in the url, JSON-encoded in the body — write "q": {query}, not "q": "{query}"). {{secret:service/label}} refs decrypt from the API-key vault at call time (list them with api_key_refs). Input fields no template consumes are sent as a JSON body (non-GET) or query params (GET). Write a precise description (the model granting agents read it) and declare every {param} in input_schema.properties. Pass group_slug to author INTO an integration group: its base URL and credential fold into the stored tool (your own headers/query win). Always api_tool_test after creating. Only http tools can be authored this way — shell tools are human-only.

slug.description: lowercase letters/digits/dash/underscore — the function name models call

name.description: display name shown in tool pickers and Settings → Tools, e.g. "Mapbox geocode"

description.description: what it does + when to use it — models read this

input_schema.description: JSON Schema for the tool input. Declare every {param} used in the templates.

url.description: http(s) URL template, may contain {param}. With group_slug a path relative to the group base URL is fine, e.g. /weather

group_slug.description: integration group this tool joins, e.g. weather-tools — the tool is added to the group and inherits its base URL + credential placement. Must already exist (`tool_group_ensure`)

body.description: body template; omit to send unconsumed input as a JSON body (query string for GET/HEAD)

requires_confirm.description: park calls for operator approval — set true for destructive endpoints (deletes, payments, sends). If the owner has "require approval for agent-built tools" on, every authored tool starts gated regardless and only the operator can clear it in Settings → Tools.

name: api_tool_update
description: Update a user-defined HTTP tool by slug. Provide only the fields to change; headers/query replace the whole map when given; body: null clears the template. Pass group_slug to (re)join an integration group — the tool is added to it and re-inherits its base URL + auth placement into the stored templates. Built-in tools only allow enabled/requires_confirm changes; shell tools cannot be edited by agents. `external_access` (see its param) opens an http tool to shared apps; on an mcp connector tool it is only the read-only mark, so close one by raising its connector's level or disabling it. Only the owner's MCP client switches it on.

slug.description: slug of the tool to update — the slug itself cannot be changed

name.description: replacement display name; omit to keep the current one

description.description: replacement description — what it does + when to use it, as in `api_tool_create`

input_schema.description: replacement JSON Schema for the tool input (the whole schema, not a merge). Declare every {param} the templates use.

url.description: replacement http(s) URL template, may contain {param}; relative to the group base URL when group_slug is given

group_slug.description: integration group this tool should belong to, e.g. weather-tools — adds it and re-applies the group base URL + credential placement

method.description: replacement HTTP method; omit to keep the current one

headers.description: replacement header → value template map — replaces the whole map ({} clears it)

query.description: replacement query key → value template map — replaces the whole map ({} clears it)

body.description: replacement body template; null clears it so unconsumed input is sent as a JSON body (query string for GET/HEAD)

requires_confirm.description: toggle the confirm gate. When the owner requires approval for agent-built tools, you can only tighten it (clearing is operator-only, in Settings → Tools).

enabled.description: set false to disable the tool without deleting it; true re-enables

external_access.description: "External access". On an http tool: true lets everyone an app that declares it is shared with (members, clients, contacts on a contact link) call it, by hand too, with any input; false closes it. On an mcp connector tool: the read-only mark only (true = reads, false = can change data); it never closes the tool, the connector's level does. Never for recipe or shell tools.

read_only_confirmed.description: with external_access: true, the admin confirms the tool only reads data (the brain cannot check an outside tool). Required to switch on.

name: api_tool_delete
description: Delete a user-defined (http/shell) tool by slug. Built-ins cannot be deleted. Check tool_group_list first — deleting a tool other agents use breaks them silently.

slug.description: slug of the user-defined tool to delete

name: api_tool_test
description: Execute an HTTP tool with the given input and return the real response — use after api_tool_create/update to prove the tool works before handing it to agents. Runs the exact dispatcher agents use (templating + vault secrets). Refuses builtin/shell tools.

slug.description: slug of the http tool to run

name: api_key_refs
description: List the encrypted API-key vault entries as {{secret:service/label}} reference strings for use in tool templates. Returns masked previews only — plaintext never leaves the vault. If the service the user wants is missing, ask them to add the key under Settings → API keys.

name: api_docs_set
description: Store (or REPLACE) an integration group's API documentation as a markdown file on this brain and point the group at it. Returns the stored size. Do this right after `web_fetch`ing a service's docs, before authoring: the next pass — any agent, months later — then reads `api_docs_get` instead of re-fetching a page that may have moved or gone behind auth. The stored copy is indexed, so every agent's `search_nodes` can find it. Keep the endpoint reference, auth scheme, parameters, and an example response; drop the marketing pages. Pass source_url so provenance is recorded.

group_slug.description: integration group these docs belong to, e.g. weather-tools

markdown.description: the documentation itself, as markdown — endpoints, auth, parameters, an example response. Replaces the whole file, so include everything you still want (read the old copy first with `api_docs_get` when you're extending)

source_url.description: where it came from, e.g. https://openweathermap.org/api/one-call-3 — recorded in the file header so a later reader can refresh it

name: api_docs_get
description: Read back the API documentation stored on an integration group — the markdown `api_docs_set` saved, in slices (pass offset to continue). **Read this FIRST when adding a call to an existing integration**: it's this brain's captured copy, so it costs nothing and can't have moved. Use `web_fetch` only when a group has no stored docs or they don't cover the endpoint you need — then `api_docs_set` the refreshed copy back. Returns has_docs false (not an error) when nothing is stored, plus where the copy came from and when it was captured, so you can judge staleness.

group_slug.description: integration group whose docs to read, e.g. weather-tools

offset.description: character offset to resume from when the previous slice was truncated

max_chars.description: size of the slice to return

name: api_skill_set
description: Write (or replace) the short USAGE skill that travels with an integration group: distilled judgment — which endpoint answers which question, unit and date conventions, how to chain two calls, how to read the response. Every agent granted the group gets this in its context on every turn, so keep it tight and never paste the reference docs in (those live in `api_docs_set`; this is what you learned USING them). Do it last, after the calls test green. Creates/updates one skill per group and links it, so calling twice revises rather than forking.

group_slug.description: integration group this skill belongs to, e.g. weather-tools

body.description: the skill in markdown, ~150–250 words: when to reach for each tool, the conventions a caller gets wrong (units, timezones, id lookups), and per-tool notes where one call needs special handling

name.description: display name for the skill, e.g. "Weather API usage" — defaults to the group name plus "usage"

name: tool_catalog
description: List the tools you can COMPOSE into a recipe tool (recipe_tool_create) — the brain's own content/search/file/page/task/journal/event/table builtins plus your authored http tools. Returns each tool's slug, kind, full description, and input_schema so you know the exact slug + input shape to chain. Excludes tools recipes may not call (terminal, secrets, delegation, the tool-authoring kit, confirm-gated, shell). Filter with q. This is how you discover the steps for a new recipe.

include_input_schema.description: include each tool's full input_schema (default true; set false for a terse list)

name: recipe_tool_create
description: Author a NEW tool by composing EXISTING tools — no external service, no code change. A recipe chains existing tools server-side — data flows between steps, never through the model. In a step's input an EXACT "{param}" pulls the recipe's own input value (any type) and an EXACT "$0" / "$name" / "$name.field" pulls a prior step's output; embedded in a longer string ("{first} {last}") they substitute as text. Use it to fill a local-capability gap (e.g. "turn a note into a page" = `note_get` → `page_create`) as one reusable, agent-callable tool. Steps may only call composable tools — browse `tool_catalog`; shell, confirm-gated, and terminal/secrets/delegation/tool-authoring tools are refused. Always `recipe_tool_test` after creating, then `tool_group_ensure` + `agent_grant_tool_group` to grant it.

slug.description: lowercase letters/digits/dash/underscore — the function name models call

name.description: display name shown in tool pickers and Settings → Tools, e.g. "Note to page"

description.description: what it does + when to use it — models read this

input_schema.description: JSON Schema for the tool input. Declare every {param} used in the steps.

tool.description: slug of an existing composable tool

input.description: input for the tool; values may use {param} and $ref templates

as.description: optional name to reference this step's output as $name (else $index)

steps.description: ordered list of { tool, input?, as? } — the tools to chain

output.description: optional output template (resolved like a step input); default = last step's output

requires_confirm.description: park calls for operator approval before running the recipe

name: recipe_tool_test
description: Run a recipe tool with the given input and return its real output — use after recipe_tool_create to prove the chain works before granting it. Runs the exact dispatcher agents use, so side effects ARE real (a recipe that creates a page will create one). Refuses non-recipe tools (use api_tool_test for http).

slug.description: slug of the recipe tool to run

name: tool_group_list
description: List tool groups (capability bundles agents are granted): slug, tool slugs, and which agents currently grant each group. A group bound to an API also reports its integration — service, base URL, vault ref, whether documentation is stored, and its usage skill. Start here when extending an existing integration: find the group, then `api_docs_get` its stored docs.

name: tool_group_ensure
description: Create a tool group if it doesn't exist, or update its tool list. mode 'add' (default) merges slugs in; 'replace' overwrites the list. Unknown tool slugs are reported as warnings, not errors. Pass `service` (+ `base_url` / `secret_ref` or `oauth2` / `auth_template`) to make the group an INTEGRATION: auth placement and the base URL are decided ONCE here, and every tool later authored with group_slug inherits them. Changing the tools of a group an assistant of another workspace than Admin holds waits for the operator's approval (Pending). Then `api_docs_set` the API documentation onto the same group so the next authoring pass reads it instead of the web.

name.description: display name (required when creating)

description.description: what the bundle is for, e.g. "Mapbox geocoding + routing"; omit to keep the existing one

tool_slugs.description: slugs of the tools the group should contain — http/recipe tools only, e.g. ["mapbox_geocode"]

service.description: vendor key for the API this group integrates, e.g. 'openweathermap' — set it (with the fields below) to turn a plain bundle into an integration

base_url.description: URL every call in this group hangs off, e.g. https://api.openweathermap.org/data/2.5 — authored tools may then use relative paths

secret_ref.description: vault entry that authenticates this API as 'service/label', e.g. openweathermap/default — list the real ones with `api_key_refs` and ask the user when two could fit

client_id_ref.description: vault ref 'service/label' of the client id

client_secret_ref.description: vault ref 'service/label' of the client secret

scope.description: space-separated scopes, if the provider wants them

audience.description: audience / resource id, if the provider wants one

client_auth.description: how the client authenticates to the token endpoint; default 'basic'

oauth2.description: OAuth2 client credentials, for APIs that hand out bearer tokens. Both credentials are vault refs (`api_key_refs`). Needs base_url. When auth_template is unset it defaults to { "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer {{oauth:<this group slug>}}" } }. Pass null to remove.

name: agent_list
description: Read-only list of the agents on this Mantle: slug, name, role, enabled, which tool groups each grants, and its thinking effort (null = inherits the profile). Use before agent_grant_tool_group or agent_set_thinking_effort.

name: agent_grant_tool_group
description: Add a tool group to an agent's grants so its tools become callable by that agent (chat turns and heartbeat fires alike). Confirm with the user which agent should receive new capabilities before granting.

agent_slug.description: agent receiving the grant — must differ from the calling agent (self-grants are refused); list candidates with `agent_list`

group_slug.description: tool group to grant; must already exist — create it with `tool_group_ensure`

name: agent_set_thinking_effort
description: Set how hard an agent reasons before it answers: 'inherit' (follow the owner's profile setting), 'off', or a tier from 'low' to 'max'. Higher tiers cost more per turn and are used only when the model supports reasoning effort. Confirm the agent and the tier with the user first. Another agent asking waits for operator approval.

agent_slug.description: agent to change; must differ from the calling agent (an agent cannot raise its own effort); list candidates with `agent_list`
